posts.title: Crane bases, AI-looking calculations and a missing temporary works procedure
posts.excerpt: This week's contractor briefing is about three control failures that still look respectable on paper: copying a CIRIA crane-base worked example without checking the tension-side shear case; accepting a polished calculation pack that was not a competent structural check; and running a site with no temporary works procedure, no Temporary Works Coordinator and no design for a wall that later collapsed into an excavation.
posts.linkedinReady:
A tower-crane base, a plant pad on an existing roof and a newly built blockwork wall next to an excavation are all temporary works. They need a brief, a competent design or accepted standard solution, a check that matches the actual load path, and a named Temporary Works Coordinator. Paper that looks finished is not the same as a structure that will stand.

Three published strands are worth putting in front of every TWC, TWS and commercial manager this week.

CROSS Report 1552 (29 June 2026) concerns Worked Example 3 in CIRIA C761, Tower crane foundation and tie design. The reporter questioned whether shear enhancement used in that example is valid on the side of a square piled crane base where overturning puts the crane leg and pile into tension. The Expert Panel generally agreed: without a compression strut, shear enhancement should not be relied on for the uplift case. Design for the full shear demand, or use a strut-and-tie model with detailing that can actually be fixed. Do not copy a worked example or a spreadsheet derived from it and assume the geometry and load path on your site are the same.

CROSS Report 1554 (16 July 2026) is about heavy plant proposed on an existing flat-slab roof. An architect submitted a detailed-looking calculation pack to justify the extra load. A reviewing structural engineer found the roof was only suitable for light plant, that the technical content was wrong, and that the pack had the hallmarks of unverified AI output - including new errors after a rapid rewrite. The Expert Panel point is blunt: AI is not a substitute for competent structural judgement. Dutyholders must stay inside their competence. Existing-structure capacity is part of the temporary works load path whenever plant, a crane or a grillage is added.

HSE December 2025 prosecution of Matrod Frampton Ltd is the procedure case. A blockwork wall at a Poole site was backfilled before the mortar had set and collapsed into an excavation, causing life-changing injuries to a steel-fixer. There was no temporary works design for the wall or for other temporary works on the site, no Temporary Works Coordinator and no Temporary Works Supervisor, even though the company's own safety consultants had flagged the gap eight days earlier. The company was fined 100000 pounds plus costs for CDM 2015 Regulations 13(1) and 19(1).

What a competent TWC should do with this:

- Treat every tower-crane base, tie, climbing frame and chocking arrangement as a bespoke temporary works item. Check tension-side shear and do not treat CIRIA C761 examples as a calculation.
- Do not accept plant, grillage or crane loads on existing fabric without a competent existing-structure assessment. A well-written PDF is not a check.
- If there is no live temporary works procedure, no named TWC and no design for walls, excavations or backfill sequence, stop that item until the project procedure says it can proceed.

Educational only - not for construction; subject to the project temporary works procedure.

body.h: CROSS 1552 - CIRIA C761 worked examples are not a crane-base design
body.p: CROSS-UK Report 1552 (published 29 June 2026) concerns Worked Example 3 in CIRIA C761, Guide to tower crane foundation and tie design. The reporter had used the example and later questioned the shear check on a square piled crane base. The example applies shear enhancement on the compression side of the base. The reporter observed that the corresponding planes on the tension side - where overturning puts the crane leg and pile reaction into tension - were not checked in the same way, and that a compression strut cannot form if both reactions are in tension. The reporter own review indicated that tension-side shear adjacent to the pile could be substantially over-utilised if enhancement is stripped out. The Expert Panel generally agreed that shear enhancement cannot be applied in that worked-example detailing when both the crane leg and the pile are in tension. A simplified approach is to design the base for the full shear demand without enhancement; alternatively a strut-and-tie analysis can be used if the detailing can be fixed on site. The Panel also warned against standardising crane-base design through spreadsheets copied from guidance examples. Crane foundations are normally single, safety-critical, project-specific elements.

body.h: CROSS 1554 - polished calculations are not a competent check of existing fabric
body.p: CROSS-UK Report 1554 (published 16 July 2026) describes a proposal to put heavy plant on the roof of a reinforced-concrete flat-slab building of fewer than seven storeys, with retail at ground floor and residential above. An architect issued a calculation report that looked detailed and included analysis figures. The reviewing structural engineer found the roof capable of supporting only light plant, existing ducts already on a steel grillage, and technical content that was factually wrong. The reporter concluded the pack was largely AI-generated, noting how quickly it was rewritten and that new errors appeared in later revisions. The Expert Panel stated that current AI systems are not known to be capable of structural engineering judgement, that LLM outputs can look authoritative while being wrong, and that checking and approval must remain with a suitably qualified and experienced structural engineer. Competence duties under Part 2A of the Building Regulations 2010 (Regulations 11F-11H) require dutyholders to stay within their expertise. For a Temporary Works Coordinator the lesson is the same as CROSS 1539: existing structure is part of the load path. Plant pads, grillages and crane bases that sit on existing fabric need an existing-structure assessment, not a well-presented file.

body.h: HSE Matrod Frampton - no procedure, no TWC, wall into an excavation
body.p: On 19 August 2022 at Old Coast Guard Road, Poole, a newly built breeze-block wall was backfilled before the mortar had set and collapsed into an excavation, crushing steel-fixer Patrick Grant against the concrete floor and causing life-changing injuries. HSE found no temporary works design for the wall or for other temporary works on the site, and no Temporary Works Coordinator or Temporary Works Supervisor, despite a safety report raising that concern eight days earlier. Without a temporary works procedure, groundworkers backfilled prematurely. Rescue was delayed by the absence of an emergency rescue plan and by use of an unstable ladder into a deep excavation. Matrod Frampton Ltd pleaded guilty to CDM 2015 Regulations 13(1) and 19(1) and was fined 100000 pounds plus 8242 pounds costs and a 2000 pound victim surcharge at Bristol Magistrates Court on 5 December 2025. HSE inspector Alexander Ashen said a temporary works procedure should have been implemented as a matter of course and that the event was wholly avoidable.

body.h: What this means on a live register this week
body.p: Put tower-crane bases, ties, climbing frames and chocking on the Temporary Works Register as bespoke items. Require the designer to show the tension-side shear case and to state whether shear enhancement has been used and why it is valid for that geometry. Treat any proposal to place plant, a grillage or a crane on existing fabric as an existing-structure temporary works problem: demand drawings, a competent assessment and a check category under the project procedure. Confirm that walls next to excavations, backfill sequence and mortar cure are designed or covered by an accepted standard solution with hold points - they are temporary works, not a groundworks habit. If the project still has no named Temporary Works Coordinator and no written procedure, that is the first hold point.
